column6: Older text: Explainer equates 50% infant mortality with "died before age 5"; Q2 lists 1831 and 1832 as separate epidemics (one 1831-32 epidemic).

Older text: Q3 says India had 40,000 rail miles by 1900 (about 24,000) and was built to British gauge (India used 5 ft 6 in broad gauge); Explainer credits the gauge to Robert rather than George Stephenson; Q1 calls Huskisson the first railway fatality (earlier deaths exist); Q4 true-false item is phrased as an open question.

Bullet 4 said the 3rd-century debasement was of the denarius; by mid-century the debased silver coin was the antoninianus. Older text: Q5 and Explainer make the same denarius slip; Q2 says 1-2 million slaves in Italy, Explainer says 2-3 million; Q1 credits Caesar and Augustus with free grain (Clodius, 58 BCE); Explainer lists Laurion as a Roman slave mine.

Bullet 1 belief is near-strawman but matches the Explainer's framing; kept. Older text: Q3 and Explainer give Manchester infant mortality as 50% (that figure fits under-5 deaths in the worst districts, not infant mortality); Q4 "36 million homes" figure is doubtful.
Older text: Q4 true-false item is phrased as an open question; Q5 conflates the welfare Matthew Effect (benefits flowing to the better-off) with the political durability of universal programs.
